page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-32 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel processor. It features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration provides 256 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 8 GB of memory per vCPU. The CPU cache hierarchy includes 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 208.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 99.59 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 44.59 GB/sec. In contrast, computational benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core (25674.63) and Geekbench multi-core (15821.0) register in the average tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like low-precision matrix multiplication.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, the n4-highmem-32 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of high memory bandwidth and dedicated CPU allocation makes this server suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale web serving, intermediate ETL processing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
